The user is Japanese, asking for design of a web app to help practice GeoGuessr. They want random Street View images, guess the country, AI evaluates guess and gives feedback, points out missed clues. Constraints: personal dev, low cost, 2 weeks, web app, can use LLM API.

We need to propose architecture, data model, AI usage, tech stack. Provide detailed design, components, flow, cost considerations, using free tiers (e.g., Google Street View API, OpenStreetMap, Mapbox, etc.), LLM like OpenAI GPT-4o or Claude. Also need to handle licensing for Street View images (Google Maps API requires billing). Perhaps use Mapillary (now part of Meta) or OpenStreetCam with free images. Also consider using OpenAI's image generation? No, need real images.

Outline:

- Frontend: React (Next.js) for SSR, TypeScript, UI library (MUI or Tailwind).
- Backend: Node.js (Express) or Next.js API routes; maybe serverless functions (Vercel).
- Database: SQLite for minimal data (user guesses, scores) or use local storage for personal use.
- Street View images: Use Google Street View Static API (cost per request) but within free tier? Or use Mapillary API (free). Provide fallback.

- Random location selection: Use list of preselected coordinate points with country labels from open dataset (e.g., Natural Earth). Or sample from world polygon data.

- Game flow:
  1. Request new round -> backend selects random coordinate, fetches static Street View image (or Mapillary image) and returns to front.
  2. UI shows image, ask user to input guess (country name or dropdown). Could also show map after guess.
  3. User submits; backend records guess, calls LLM with prompt: image description (maybe we send image URL to LLM, but LLM can't see image). Use vision-capable LLM (OpenAI's GPT-4V) to analyze image and compare guess. Provide feedback: list of clues, what was missed.
  4. Return feedback to frontend for display.

- LLM usage: Use GPT-4V (image+text) or Claude 3 Opus with image input. Provide system prompt to detect clues: signs, language, vegetation, infrastructure, vehicle side, license plates, etc. Provide evaluation logic.

- For cost: limit to e.g., 10 rounds per session, caching images, using low-resolution images.

- Data model: Users (if any), Sessions, Rounds (timestamp, location, image_url, correct_country, user_guess, score, feedback). Maybe SQLite tables.

- Security: Keep API keys server-side.

- Deployment: Vercel or Netlify (serverless functions). Use environment variables for API keys.

- Timeline: Week 1: set up project, integrate Street View API, design DB, UI skeleton. Week 2: integrate LLM, feedback generation, polishing, deploy.

Provide details for each component, sample code snippets for API calls, prompts for LLM.

Also optional: Add hint system: user can ask for clue, system reveals e.g., language of sign, driving side.

Add ability to store performance over time (graph). Use chart library.

Provide cost estimation.
